title: BOOKKEEPER — AUSTRALIAN FAMILY OFFICE (Remote)
description:
BOOKKEEPER — AUSTRALIAN FAMILY OFFICE



Part-time remote, from the Philippines. Overlapping Melbourne business hours. Above-market pay. Long-term. Direct to the Principal.



This is a rare bookkeeping role with a kind, well-respected Australian entrepreneur — the kind of person you'll genuinely enjoy working for. You'll be the trusted bookkeeping hand across his family office, his operating businesses, and his investments. No middle layer, no churn, no being treated like a disposable freelancer. A long-term seat at the table, above-market pay, and real responsibility from day one.





Why this role



You'll work directly with the Principal. No project manager in between. Your work goes straight to the person it matters to.



A Principal worth working for. A well-respected Australian entrepreneur with a family office, operating businesses, investments, and family trusts — heavy focus in the health and medical industry. Kind, responsible, and approachable. The kind of client you'll want to do a great job for.



Above-market pay, reliably on time. This is not a budget hire.



Long-term and stable. A trusted bookkeeping hand he plans to keep for years, not a short contract.



Interesting variety. Multiple entities across Australia and New Zealand — investment holding, operating businesses, family trusts, and the Principal's personal accounts. You'll see how a real family office runs.



Real growth. The role can grow into payroll, deeper reporting, and process improvement as the engagement matures.



Respected and trusted. You'll be brought into the inner circle of someone's financial life — that trust is the role.





Role purpose



The Bookkeeper provides hands-on day-to-day bookkeeping in QuickBooks Online — payments and bills, monthly reconciliation, GST/BAS preparation, and consolidated reporting that gives the Principal a clean view across all entities.





The team you'll work with



A small, high-trust circle: the Principal himself, his external Australian accountant (who picks up at EOFY), and you. No layers, no committees. You'll be in regular direct contact with the Principal — a brief call, a chat message, a tidy monthly report. The kind of working relationship that gets better year on year.





Key responsibilities



Day-to-day bookkeeping. Code and enter transactions in QuickBooks Online across multiple entities (debits and credits, expense categorisation, bill entry, receipts capture). Maintain a clean, well-organised chart of accounts for each entity. File and attach supporting documents to transactions. Flag unusual transactions or missing source documents.



Accounts payable and receivable. Process incoming invoices: review, code, enter into QuickBooks, prepare for payment. Action outgoing payments on the Principal's instruction across the relevant entities. Track inter-entity reimbursements (e.g. one entity pays an invoice and recovers from another) and keep the audit trail clean. Maintain supplier records and follow up on missing or incorrect invoices. Issue and track customer invoices where required.



Reconciliation and month-end. Reconcile bank, credit card, and loan accounts monthly across all entities. Resolve discrepancies. Close the books at month-end and produce a tidy trial balance. Maintain a simple month-end checklist so each entity closes consistently.



GST, BAS, and compliance preparation. Prepare GST/BAS workings for the Australian entities; depending on the engagement, either lodge through QuickBooks or hand off to the Principal's accountant. Maintain accurate GST coding throughout the period — not just at BAS time. Keep records audit-ready for the accountant's end-of-financial-year review.



Reporting. Produce monthly P&L and Balance Sheet for each entity. Produce a simple consolidated view across the Principal's interests. Highlight notable movements, large items, or anything that doesn't look right. Respond to ad-hoc queries from the Principal (e.g. "what did we spend on X this quarter").



Engagement and communication. Provide regular updates and reporting. Timely responses and turnarounds. Be available within agreed working hours. Maintain confidentiality across all personal and business financial information.





What we're looking for



We're hiring for craft, judgement, and trust — not a checklist. If most of the below describes you, please apply.



5+ years of hands-on bookkeeping experience, including full reconciliation and month-end close.



Strong working knowledge of QuickBooks Online, including multi-entity setups.



Solid Australian context — confident with Australian GST, BAS, and ATO conventions. This is the one non-negotiable.



Comfortable working across multiple entities and account sets in parallel without losing track.



Strong attention to detail, organised, accurate.



High standard of written and spoken English — able to write a clear, concise update and hold a conversation with the Principal on a call.



Discreet and trustworthy with sensitive personal and business financial information.



Self-motivated; able to work independently without close supervision.



Reliable home internet and a dedicated, professional home workspace.



Nice to have (not required): experience supporting Australian small-business or family-office clients; familiarity with New Zealand GST treatment (one of the entities is NZ-based); payroll experience (the role may expand to include payroll later); experience preparing files for an external accountant to finalise at EOFY; comfort suggesting small process improvements as the engagement matures.





Who you are



You take pride in clean books. You like the quiet satisfaction of a month-end that closes cleanly, a BAS that ties out first time, a chart of accounts that someone else could pick up tomorrow and understand. You're trustworthy with sensitive information. You communicate proactively — no chasing required. And you'd rather have one good long-term client you genuinely respect than five chaotic ones.



If that sounds like you, we'd love to meet you.





How to Apply



Apply directly via OJP. Attach:



1. Your resume (PDF), including the QuickBooks Online environments you've worked in and the countries/tax jurisdictions you've supported.



In your application message, answer these three questions. Short, direct answers — no AI fluff.



1. Australian context. Walk us through how you handled GST coding and BAS prep for an Australian client in your most recent role — coding discipline through the period, what you reconciled at BAS time, and how you handed off to the external accountant. This is essential, not desirable.



2. Multi-entity discipline. How many separate entities (companies / trusts / personal) have you bookkept in QuickBooks Online in parallel, and how do you keep inter-entity reimbursements and the consolidated view clean without losing the audit trail?



3. Logistics. Expected hourly rate in PHP for part-time hours (tell us the hours per week you're targeting), earliest start date, and confirm you can overlap Melbourne, Australia business hours each working day.



Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

title: Travel, Procurement & Fleet Coordinator
description:
Who is Bare?

Bare is the new way to funeral. We are a holistic end of life care provider, allowing our families to grieve in their own way, at their own pace, knowing their loved one is cared for by a team who truly understand their needs.



By combining empathy with technology, we’re creating end-of-life experiences that are simple, personalized and affordable. In only five years, we’ve served more than 30,000 families, have become Australia’s most awarded end-of-life provider (with awards in customer service, innovation and digital disruption), and have built a team of more than 100 people committed to changing the way Australians deal with end-of-life. And we’re just getting started.

Position Overview

We are seeking a highly organized, proactive, and detail-oriented Travel, Procurement & Fleet Coordinator to manage operations for our Australian business. This multi-faceted role is critical to maintaining seamless daily logistics. You will be responsible for orchestrating domestic and corporate travel, managing supplier procurement in line with local compliance, and assisting with the maintenance and safety of our corporate fleet.

The ideal candidate understands the Australian vendor landscape, has experience managing corporate travel across ANZ, and brings a strong customer-service focus to supporting our local workforce.



Key Responsibilities

1. Travel Management (Approx. 40%)

Booking & Domestic Logistics: Coordinate extensive corporate travel bookings across Australia (interstate) including flights (Qantas, Virgin Australia, Jetstar), corporate accommodation, and car rentals.

Policy Compliance: Enforce the company’s travel and expense policy, ensuring cost-efficient booking habits and appropriate tier selections.



TMC & Platform Management: Act as the primary administrator for the corporate travel management platform (e.g., Corporate Traveller, FCM, or Serko) and handle corporate profile updates.



Fringe Benefits Tax (FBT) & Expense Alignment: Support the Finance team by ensuring travel expenses are accurately categorized to assist with FBT reporting and tracking meals/entertainment allowances.



2. Procurement & Supplier Relations (Approx. 40%)

Local Sourcing: Raise purchase requisitions and manage the end-to-end purchase order (PO) process for Australian suppliers, covering office supplies, IT equipment, and operational materials.



Vendor Management: Onboard new vendors, track supplier performance, and maintain compliant records including valid Australian Business Numbers (ABNs) and GST status verification.



Payment Lifecycle Collaboration: Reconcile invoices against delivery receipts and POs, liaising closely with the Accounts Payable team to ensure adherence to agreed payment terms.



Modern Slavery Act Compliance: Assist the procurement team in verifying supplier compliance in alignment with corporate social responsibility guidelines and local Modern Slavery reporting frameworks.



3. Fleet Management Assistance (Approx. 20%)

Asset Tracking & Registration: Maintain an updated corporate fleet registry, ensuring all vehicle registrations (via relevant state bodies like VicRoads, Transport for NSW, TMR, etc.) and compulsory third-party (CTP) insurances are systematically renewed.



Maintenance & Safety: Coordinate scheduled logbook servicing, tyre replacements, and vehicle inspections to maintain fleet safety and uphold manufacturer warranties.



Fuel Cards & Linkt/E-Toll Management: Monitor corporate fuel card accounts (e.g., Ampol, BP, Shell) and toll account usage (e.g., Linkt), reporting on weekly or monthly variances.



I
 Management: Assist drivers with a
 reporting processes, insurance claims documentation, and coordinating roadside assistance when required.



Qualifications & Skills

Experience: 2–4 years of experience in an operations, procurement, or corporate travel coordination role within Australia. Previous exposure to vehicle fleet coordination or logistics is highly regarded.



Technical Systems: Proficiency with ERP/financial software (e.g., Xero, MYOB, SAP, NetSuite), expense management tools, and corporate travel software (e.g., Velocity, Concur).



Regulatory Understanding: Familiarity with Australian business operational requirements, including GST invoicing principles, state-based vehicle registration rules, and basic workplace safety requirements.



Communication & Negotiation: Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with a collaborative approach to handling internal staff requests and local vendor negotiations.



Problem-Solving: Strong situational awareness with the ability to resolve rapid shifts in logistics, such as travel disruptions or freight delays.



What We Offer

Competitive salary package.

Collaborative team environment with hybrid working flexibility.

Clear pathways for professional growth and career progression across the operations and procurement functions.



Please include a link to your resume for review.

Job Type: Full-Time, 40 hours per week. 



Schedule: Monday through Friday. Must be available and working during US Eastern time zone business hours, 9am to 5pm ET. You will be working night shift Philippines time. Candidates who have done this before are strongly preferred. Compensation: Based on experience, discussed during interview. Weekly pay. 12-month contract with strong renewal potential. Start Date: As soon as possible.



Who We Are

We are a US-based real estate investor, Realtor, and systems builder operating in Central Florida. The founder is an active real estate investor specializing in fix and flip projects, a licensed real estate agent serving investor clients



We manage a rental portfolio, work with fix and flip investors, and are actively building a personal brand across YouTube, LinkedIn, Instagram, and other platforms. This is a fast-moving, high-activity operation, and we need someone who can keep the back end running and the brand growing so the founder can focus on deals and content strategy.



What This Role Is

This role evolves in two clear phases over the 12-month contract. We want someone who can grow with us, not just fill a seat.

Phase one covers approximately the first 30 to 60 days. Your primary focus is rental leasing operations — managing leads, following up relentlessly, and moving prospects through the pipeline from first inquiry through signed lease. Once the portfolio is fully leased, this workload largely goes away.

Phase two begins as the portfolio stabilizes. Your focus shifts to systems building, investor and buyer support, and social media and YouTube content operations. This is where the role grows into something more strategic and more interesting for the right candidate.

If you are someone who wants to learn real estate investing, CRM automation, content operations, and brand building from the inside of a growing multi-brand operation, this role will develop you fast.



Your Responsibilities



Phase One — Rental Leasing Operations (first 30 to 60 days, primary focus):

Respond to all new rental inquiries via text,
, and phone using approved scripts

Qualify rental prospects by phone using provided criteria

Schedule showings on the showing assistant's calendar

Send showing confirmations and reminders

Follow up persistently with leads and applicants who go quiet

Manage the full prospect pipeline in GoHighLevel CRM from first contact through signed lease

Collect, organize, and track application documents in Google Drive

Send applications, contracts, and checklists to qualified prospects

Update all rental listings across Zillow, TurboTenant,
 Marketplace, and
 Groups

Monitor listing inboxes across all platforms

Prepare weekly pipeline and vacancy status reports



Phase Two — Systems, Investor Support, and Brand Operations (ongoing and expanding):

CRM and Systems:

Build and manage workflows and automations in GoHighLevel

Build and maintain task structures, templates, and workflows in ClickUp

Build and monitor automation scenarios in 

Manage investor and buyer leads in CRM: enter contacts, update pipeline stages, log notes

Send follow-up messages to investor and homeowner leads using approved scripts

Coordinate calls and appointments between the founder and clients

Organize deal documents and correspondence in Google Drive

Pull weekly reports from GHL and summarize in plain language

Content and Social Media Operations:

Manage the content calendar in ClickUp across all platforms

Schedule and publish approved content on LinkedIn, Instagram,
, and TikTok using scheduling tools

Support YouTube production operations: organize video files, manage upload schedules, draft descriptions and tags using provided direction

Monitor comments and messages across platforms, flag priority items for founder response

Track weekly engagement metrics and compile a simple report: reach, followers, saves, shares, views

Repurpose long-form content into short-form captions and clip descriptions as directed



Administrative:

Manage daily tasks and priorities in ClickUp

Monitor the dedicated operations
 inbox

Draft routine
 and message responses for founder review and approval

Organize files and documents in Google Drive

Schedule and confirm appointments on the founder's calendar



What We Are Looking For:



Required:

Phone confidence in English. You will be calling and receiving calls from US-based rental prospects, tenants, vendors, contractors, and investors. Your spoken English must be clear and professional. This will be evaluated in your Loom video and confirmed in the interview. Candidates from BPO or US-facing call center backgrounds are strongly encouraged to apply.

Systems and automation experience. You must have hands-on experience building or managing workflows in at least one of the following: GoHighLevel, 
, ClickUp automations, or a comparable CRM automation tool. Knowing how to use a tool is not enough. We need someone who has built something in it. Be specific in your application about what you built.

Follow-through without being reminded. This operation has many open items running simultaneously. Leads that do not get followed up fall through. Vendors that are not chased miss deadlines. You close every loop. We need a specific real example from your work history, not a general claim.

Project management tool experience. ClickUp, Asana, Monday, or equivalent. You will live in ClickUp daily.

Detail orientation you can prove with a specific story. 

Reliable fast internet and a quiet dedicated workspace for calls. Non-negotiable.

Strongly preferred:

GoHighLevel experience specifically. Pipelines, workflows, automations, campaigns, and conversation management.


 experience. Building multi-step scenarios, not just connecting two apps.

Social media scheduling and content operations experience. Meta Business Suite, social media scheduling tools. 

Real estate experience of any kind. Property management, leasing, investor support, mortgage, title, or transaction coordination.

Experience supporting a US-based entrepreneur or small business owner directly.



Bonus Skills That Will Make You Stand Out

These are not required to apply. Candidates who have any of the following will have a meaningful advantage and should highlight them clearly in their Loom video and written summary:

Spanish fluency. We work with a large Spanish-speaking investor, tenant, vendor, and buyer population in Central Florida. A bilingual candidate is a significant operational asset.

Canva or basic graphic design. Ability to produce clean one-pagers, deal flyers, and social media graphics from existing templates without needing a separate designer.

YouTube channel management. Experience with upload workflows, SEO-optimized descriptions, tags, thumbnails coordination, and channel analytics.

Transaction coordination familiarity. Basic understanding of what happens between a real estate contract and closing — document collection, timeline tracking, lender and title communication.

Video editing basics. Ability to do simple cuts, captions, and formatting in CapCut, DaVinci Resolve, or a comparable tool.

If you have any of these, tell us specifically in your Loom video. It will strengthen your application considerably.



What This Role Offers

Direct access to the founder with no management layers between you. A 12-month contract with real stability and strong renewal potential. Weekly pay. A role that grows with you — phase one builds your operational foundation, phase two puts you at the center of a brand that is actively being built. If you want to grow your skills in real estate operations, CRM automation, and content production for a personal brand in the real estate investing space, this role will develop you fast.



How to Apply

Do not send a generic application. Do not use AI to write your cover message. Applications that do not follow these exact instructions will not be reviewed.



Submit the following two things:

One — A Loom video, 3 to 5 minutes maximum. Answer these three questions in the video:

Tell me about a role where you made or received calls in English to US clients, tenants, customers, or vendors. What were the calls about and how did you handle a situation where the person on the other end was frustrated, confused, or unresponsive?

Tell me about something specific you built in a CRM or automation tool. Not something you managed or used — something you actually built. Walk me through what it was and how it worked.

How do you stay organized when you are managing many open follow-ups across different people and different topics simultaneously? Give me a real example.

Two — A one-paragraph written summary of your most relevant experience for this role. Write it in your own words.

Applications without the Loom video will not be reviewed.

title: Operations & Project Manager (Fast Growing)
description:
This role is for that special person who wants to become truly exceptional. If that’s you, you already know this message is your signal.



Operations Manager-Execution Partner-Project Killer-Fast-Growing Comic Book Company

Own the operations backbone of a niche comic book brand, work directly with leadership, and get promoted fairly by numbers. 



What You Get If You Win Here

- High autonomy: once you’re ramped, you own your queue, schedule, and methods as long as the KPIs are hit. Lots of freedom to figure it out, great for someone that loves building with Legos

- Direct proximity to leadership: you work daily with the Ops Manager on the most important projects in the company.

- Clear advancement path: your growth is tied to visible numbers (tasks shipped, zero-miss cadence, freed founder/ops time, profit/leading metrics), not politics.

- Insane skill growth: the pace and standards here mean every 12 months with us will feel like 3 years of experience in a normal VA/ops role. You can leapfrog your friends. If you join this will change your life. You will work harder than you’ve ever worked before and grow faster than you’ve ever grown before. 

- Comic Books!: you’re not just pushing random SaaS tickets; you’re inside a real comic book store seeing rare old comic books, private deals, and the business behind the Hollywood Marvel Movies that everyone loves!

If you’re that person who enjoys working really hard to the point that it takes 2-3 people to do what you did listen up: 

Our tasks in asana for projects and ongoing operations are moving at a snail’s pace.

Ops Manager + CEO is chasing tasks, slack policing, cleaning up Asana, and re-explaining context instead of focusing on their jobs.



We’ve had “pleasant” VAs who:

Can’t drive tasks to completion independently

Mark tasks complete with no proof

Miss reports/skip cadence and require chasing. 

Drift on ownership, urgency & follow thru

Need hand-holding 

I don’t need another task hopper. I need a project killer who comes into ambiguity, creates structure, drives tasks to completion, and actually frees the Ops Manager to focus on his key projects. If this works, his deep work hours and project output go up because you’re handling everything else. We will measure that and tie your promotions/raises to it. This is not for everyone. We’re looking for winners. 



What You’ll Actually Do

You will be Ops Manager’s execution partner and force-multiplier. Concrete outputs:

Own Asana: every task has an owner, due date, Done Check, and proof link when completed

Maintain an active queue of 20+ meaningful tasks, prioritized against our key rocks (Marketing, Sales, Ongoing Operations, Cleanup, Admin)

Ship 25+ tasks/week with proof, minimal rework, and zero “ghosted” items

Proactively handle operational issues/fires in designated lanes

Maintain Reporting at Set Cadence, Follow-up loops across projects

Add leverage: plug AI into our workflows (Asana, docs, reports) to make us faster and cleaner without being asked

We do NOT need more SOPS-although you might tighten them on the fly. We need someone to do the operations. If you want to sit and write playbooks all day, this is the wrong seat-that will be an earned responsibility later. If you aren’t ready to work hard daily do not apply. 



How We Set You Up To Win (First 90 Days)

We don’t just throw you in the deep end. In your first 30 days, you’ll shadow the Ops Manager, learn our Asana + reporting systems, and get a clear scorecard so you always know what “great” looks like. By 30 days, you’ll own your own project lanes with weekly 1:1s for feedback, support, and removing blockers so you can move faster instead of guessing what we want.



Real Growth Example 

One of our Filipino teammates started with us on basic execution work at ~$800/month. Over time, he took ownership of his queue, fixed broken processes, and became the person we trusted to “just handle it.” As his scope grew, so did his comp and stability. Eight years later he makes ~$2,500/month (and we’re working on getting him even more) because he stuck with it and actually grew. A lot of people say they want that, but their resumes show 6–12 month hops. The pattern here is simple: prove you can own outcomes over time, and we grow your responsibilities, trust, and pay accordingly.



Schedule, Hours & Time Zone (No Surprises)

This is a full time, US hours role (roughly US Eastern business hours) with a true 50–60 hour workweek during this growth season. Expect most weeks to be closer to that 60 hour mark. If you want a strict 40 hour cap, this is the wrong seat; if you want a place where extra effort is noticed, measured, and rewarded, you’ll feel at home here. This is not just a job. This is a commitment.



What Winning Looks Like

By Day 30: Ops Manager is spending ~95% of his time on projects, not Slack/Asana/admin fires, because you’re handling those and executing projects alongside him. Profit and leading metrics are moving up faster because of you



By 12 months: You are Ops Manager’s go to operator & on track to become Ops Manager. Nothing important moves in Ops without you knowing. You own the Asana board, key ops projects, and reporting cadence. You’re the person we trust to “just handle it,” and your comp reflects that increased ownership. 



If you become that go to operator, you’ll have real say in how we run Ops – you won’t just be ‘executing tickets,’ you’ll help design the system.”



Who This Is NOT For

You prefer to ‘coordinate’ and assign tasks to others instead of doing the work yourself with excellence.

You want to manage people before you’ve truly proven you can personally execute at a high level. 

You want a chill, low-pressure 9–5

You need to be told what to do all day and hate being judged by objective numbers

You mark tasks complete without proof or next steps

You change jobs every 6–18 months and blame the company/manager/market/

You get defensive or freeze when given direct feedback or pressure

You are currently juggling multiple full?time clients and want to “squeeze us in” on the side.

You are mass?applying to dozens of jobs and just want to see who bites first.





Who This IS For

You’ve stayed 2–3+ years in at least one role and can prove outcomes

You like pressure, highly competitive environments, being the one who “gets it done” when others stall

You’ve built systems (trackers, automations, SOPs), not just followed them

You are tech-comfortable: Asana (or similar), CRMs, zaps, AI tools, simple web/ops/marketing stacks

You’re willing to bet on one company instead of juggling lots of smaller, easier gigs.

You’re happy to grind 50–60 hours/week no issues. We’re in a BIG growth & push season. It will be like this for the next year and then we’ll see. Everyone wants to grow a lot, but it’s actually happening here.  



Comp & Growth

Comp: Starting base $600–$700, with performance bonuses that take you to $900+ when you consistently hit + beat KPIs.” 

Raises and benefits are tied directly to beating KPIs, & raising the standard, not time served

If you crush it, scope grows into higher-level ops ownership and comp follows output

The Filipino teammate in the story above is now at ~$2,500/month and on the way up (and your growth trajectory will be much faster if you earn it because of strong systems, much better leadership, and I know what the fuck we’re doing). There is no ceiling here, this is not a forever $800 grind. But you have to earn it.  



Important: This is an ON FIELD role. You will not have a team under you to delegate to. 

95% of your time is doing the work yourself, 5% is light coordination. If your default mode is to make plans and pass tasks to others, this will be a bad fit. 

How To Apply (24-Hour Test)

Our Hiring Process (So There Are No Surprises)



If your 24 hour answers impress us, the next steps are:

A short interview focused on your past execution.

A live 60 minute work trial inside our real tools where you’ll work directly with the Ops Manager. We do this because talk is cheap. If you don’t like being tested on real work before getting hired, this won’t be a fit.



Do NOT click quick-apply. In the next 24 hours, you must:



Reply with answers to ALL of these (short but specific; bullets are fine):

Q1: Describe the most complex project you personally drove fro
ssy start to completion where you did most of the execution yourself, not just assigning tasks. Include at least one example of how you set your own deadlines and moved forward when other people were slow to respond.” 

Q2: Share 3 links or screenshots (Google Docs, Sheets, Asana boards, trackers, automations, etc.) that you built yourself which show how you organize and drive work. Briefly explain each.

Q3: You have 30 tasks due this week and realize you’ll miss 5. Walk me through, step-by-step, how you handle it with your manager and stakeholders.

Q4:  Below are 6 messy “tasks” we actually see (all dumped into one list):

– “Fix Asana, it’s a mess”

– “Seller lead texting follow up??”

– “Finance com/projections cadence d2 ”

– “Inventory backlog insane”

– “Need better reporting”

– “Update SOPs

In this role you will NOT have anyone to delegate to assume it’s just you and the Ops Manager.

In a Google Doc, please:



Rewrite these into clear tasks with: Owner (you or Ops Manager), Due Date (next 7–30 days), and a concrete Done Check + proof required. “Write your task descriptions as if you are committing: ‘I will do X by Y time. If Z doesn’t happen by [time], here’s my fallback.’ Generic ‘follow up / request access’ answers will fail you.” 

Put them in the order you’d actually do them and explain why in 3–5 bullet points.

Link the Google Doc here (view access).

Spend no more than 30–45 minutes. If you can’t figure this out on your own, this role will be too hard in real life – that’s okay, just skip applying.



Attach your PDF resume/Google Drive link.



Compensation here is performance based. Raises are earned through clearly exceeding KPIs and demonstrating core values consistently. If you want “stability” to mean “I can coast and still get raises,” this won’t feel stable. If you want stability to mean “the better I get, the more valuable and secure I become,” you’ll like it here.

title: Acquisition Research Assistant
description:
We are seeking a highly capable research assistant to support acquisition sourcing, broker outreach and pipeline management.



This is not an admin role. We need someone who can work independently, communicate professionally with brokers and manage the process with discretion and attention to detail.



This is a long-term opportunity for the right person, with scope to grow as the role develops.



Responsibilities

 - Research broker sites, marketplaces and directories to identify acquisition opportunities that fit our criteria

 - Contact brokers to request IMs and follow up when needed

 - Maintain an accurate pipeline in spreadsheets or CRM

 - Filter out weak opportunities and escalate only relevant deals

 - Provide short summaries of stronger opportunities

 - Over time, help summarise IMs and extract key data



What we're looking for:

 - Strong research skills and good judgment

 - Confident written English and a professional tone

 - Persistent, organised and detail-oriented

 - Proactive and able to work with minimal hand-holding

 - Commercially aware and discreet



Ideal experience

 - Acquisition sourcing, business brokerage, lead generation or market research

 - Comfortable reviewing basic financial information

 - Experience with spreadsheets or structured tracking systems



Growth opportunity

If you perform well, the role can grow into deal analysis, including summarising IMs, extracting key data, spotting risks and comparing opportunities.



Not suitable for:

 - Routine admin-only candidates

 - People who need constant direction

 - Anyone uncomfortable with broker follow-up

 - Candidates who want a passive support role



Pay and process

This is a paid role at a higher rate for the right person, reflecting the level of ownership expected.



How to apply

Please send a brief cover letter including:

 - Your experience with research, sourcing or lead generation

 - An example of how you manage ongoing work

 - Why this role is a good fit for you

Please start your application with “ACQUISITION”.



Shortlisted candidates will complete a paid 30–60 minute research task as part of the interview process.

title: Copywriter / Social Media Specialist Wanted!
description:
We are looking for a Copywriter / Social Media Specialist to join our team!



About the Role:

We are looking for a creative and detail-oriented Copywriter / Social Media Specialist to manage our online presence across key platforms. This role is responsible for planning, writing, and publishing engaging content while maintaining a consistent brand voice and messaging.



The role also includes copywriting for social media posts and ads, so we are looking for someone who can create content that is not only engaging but also supports campaign goals and audience growth.



Key Responsibilities:

• Manage social media platforms such as
, Instagram, and TikTok

• Plan, write, and publish engaging content for social media posts

• Write clear and compelling copy for ads, captions, hooks, and promotional content

• Maintain posting schedules and ensure brand consistency across platforms

• Support content planning for campaigns, promotions, and audience engagement

• Track content performance and engagement metrics

• Write and send

title: Part-Time Xero Expert / Bookkeeper
description:
About the Role



We are looking for an experienced and highly capable Xero Expert to join our team on a part-time basis. This role is ideal for someone who lives and breathes Xero, enjoys solving problems, and takes pride in maintaining accurate financial records.



You will be responsible for managing the day-to-day bookkeeping and finance administration functions across our New Zealand and Australian businesses, ensuring financial data is accurate, up to date, and reliable.



Key Responsibilities



Xero Administration



* Manage all day-to-day bookkeeping functions within Xero.

* Reconcile bank accounts, credit cards, and payment platforms.

* Process accounts payable and accounts receivable.

* Manage customer and supplier invoices, credit notes, and refunds.

* Maintain accurate financial records and ensure data integrity.

* Investigate and resolve reconciliation discrepancies.



E-Commerce & Payment Reconciliation



* Reconcile transactions from Shopify and other payment platforms.

* Ensure accurate matching of sales, payments, fees, and settlements.

* Assist with inventory and sales reporting where required.



Payroll & Compliance



* Process payroll accurately and on time.

* Assist with GST preparation and filing.

* Support year-end accounting requirements and external accountants.

* Ensure compliance with New Zealand and Australian financial obligations.



Financial Reporting



* Prepare monthly management reports.

* Generate and analyse Profit & Loss, Balance Sheet, and Cash Flow reports.

* Assist with budgeting, forecasting, and financial analysis.

* Provide insights and recommendations based on financial data.

* Managing financial dashboard



Cross-Business Financial Management



* Manage and reconcile financial records across both New Zealand and Australian Xero organisations.

* Ensure consistency of processes and reporting across both entities.

* Support financial decision-making through accurate and timely reporting.



About You



You are a highly organised finance professional with strong technical Xero knowledge and excellent attention to detail. You enjoy identifying issues, finding solutions, and improving processes.



Essential Skills & Experience



* Minimum 3–5 years' hands-on experience using Xero in a bookkeeping or finance role.

* Advanced knowledge of the Xero platform and its reporting capabilities.

* Strong experience with bank reconciliations, accounts payable, accounts receivable, payroll, and GST.

* Experience reconciling e-commerce platforms and payment gateways, including Shopify.

* Advanced Excel and/or Google Sheets skills.

* Exceptional attention to detail and accuracy.

* Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities.

* Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

* Ability to work independently and manage competing priorities.



Desirable



* Experience working across multiple entities or countries.

* Experience in inventory-based or e-commerce businesses.

* Knowledge of Australian accounting and GST requirements.

* Work Mon - Thursday



What We Offer



* Part-time hours.

* Opportunity to work with a growing business.

* Varied and interesting work across New Zealand and Australia.

* A collaborative team environment where accuracy, initiative, and problem-solving are highly valued.

* Fun!



If you are a true Xero expert who enjoys taking ownership of financial processes and helping businesses run smoothly, we'd love to hear from you.

title: Sales Representative
description:
Join a fast-growing US online home goods retailer and enjoy the learning and opportunities that you have while working with us.

Your work week will be 5 days per week, with 2 days off per week. Days off will be selected with your manager. We will try to accommodate your preferences for which days you like, based on availability.



This role starts ASAP!!



Job Duties and Responsibilities:

Receive incoming phone calls and live chats from potential customers (prospects) who indicated that they need shopping assistance. This does not include calls and chats from existing customers that need help with their orders (that’s a job for a different department)

Makes follow-up calls, writes follow-up
s, and text messages to potential buyers. We try to follow up 5x with each person that contacted us (unless they indicate that they are no longer interested). We don’t do cold calling. Only reaching out to prospects who interacted with our online store and left their contact information.

After each interaction with a prospect/customer, writes notes & comments in our CRM (Asana)

Communicate efficiently and build rapport with potential customers

Assists prospects in their shopping journey and helps make the purchase decision

Ensures that all prospects’ questions and objections are addressed

Leads every interaction to a close sale, which means an order is placed on our online store

Prepares custom quotes, price matches competitors if necessary, and offers custom discounts. This requires calculating margins & ensuring profitability.

Answering questions about the products we offer, including technical questions. Learns the specifications, features and benefits of our bestsellers. Over time, becomes an expert in the industry.

If not able to answer product-specific questions, conducts research in the materials provided by the supplier, or reaches out to the supplier to get the information

Confirms stock availability and lead times when offering products to prospects

Documents standard procedures and best practices in a written form, so that other tea
mbers can learn from them



Requirements:

At least 2 years of experience in sales on the phone

Experience must include both inbound and outbound sales

Excellent written and verbal English communication skills

Experience in Customer Service on the phone is a nice to have

Experience in the e-commerce (online shopping) industry is nice to have

Home improvement, construction, and gas plumbing industry experience is a plus

Outgoing, friendly, and lively

Can-do mindset, with a sense of ownership, pride in your performance, and its impact on the company’s success

Long-term commitment - treat this as your career



What we can offer:

Sales commission: 8% of gross profit from all orders closed. Gross profit means the sale amount minus the product and shipping costs. Paid monthly. No upper limit. Monthly commission payouts range between $1,200 (the guaranteed minimum) and as high as $3,000 (for the top performer). The average monthly payout is $1,465 (average from the last 2 years).

$1,200/month minimum guaranteed pay

15 days paid days off per year (also convertible to min. guaranteed commission)

Paid training on all aspects of the role

Opportunities for professional development

Friendly atmosphere

Online Interview process

Fully remote position

title: Executive Operations Assistant/Project Manager (US Time)
description:
This role is for that special person who wants to become truly exceptional. If that’s you, you already know this message is your signal.



Operations Manager-Execution Partner-Project Killer-Fast-Growing Comic Book Company

Own the operations backbone of a niche comic book brand, work directly with leadership, and get promoted fairly by numbers. 



This role is for that special person who wants to become truly exceptional. If that’s you, you already know this message is your signal.



What You Get If You Win Here

- High autonomy: once you’re ramped, you own your queue, schedule, and methods as long as the KPIs are hit. Lots of freedom to figure it out, great for someone that loves building with Legos

- Direct proximity to leadership: you work daily with the Ops Manager on the most important projects in the company.

- Clear advancement path: your growth is tied to visible numbers (tasks shipped, zero-miss cadence, freed founder/ops time, profit/leading metrics), not politics.

- Insane skill growth: the pace and standards here mean every 12 months with us will feel like 3 years of experience in a normal VA/ops role. You can leapfrog your friends. If you join this will change your life. You will work harder than you’ve ever worked before and grow faster than you’ve ever grown before. 

- Comic Books!: you’re not just pushing random SaaS tickets; you’re inside a real comic book store seeing rare old comic books, private deals, and the business behind the Hollywood Marvel Movies that everyone loves!

If you’re that person who enjoys working really hard to the point that it takes 2-3 people to do what you did listen up: 

Our tasks in asana for projects and ongoing operations are moving at a snail’s pace.

Ops Manager + CEO is chasing tasks, slack policing, cleaning up Asana, and re-explaining context instead of focusing on their jobs.



We’ve had “pleasant” VAs who:

Can’t drive tasks to completion independently

Mark tasks complete with no proof

Miss reports/skip cadence and require chasing. 

Drift on ownership, urgency & follow thru

Need hand-holding 

I don’t need another task hopper. I need a project killer who comes into ambiguity, creates structure, drives tasks to completion, and actually frees the Ops Manager to focus on his key projects. If this works, his deep work hours and project output go up because you’re handling everything else. We will measure that and tie your promotions/raises to it. This is not for everyone. We’re looking for winners. 



What You’ll Actually Do

You will be Ops Manager’s execution partner and force-multiplier. Concrete outputs:

Own Asana: every task has an owner, due date, Done Check, and proof link when completed

Maintain an active queue of 20+ meaningful tasks, prioritized against our key rocks (Marketing, Sales, Ongoing Operations, Cleanup, Admin)

Ship 25+ tasks/week with proof, minimal rework, and zero “ghosted” items

Proactively handle operational issues/fires in designated lanes

Maintain Reporting at Set Cadence, Follow-up loops across projects

Add leverage: plug AI into our workflows (Asana, docs, reports) to make us faster and cleaner without being asked

We do NOT need more SOPS-although you might tighten them on the fly. We need someone to do the operations. If you want to sit and write playbooks all day, this is the wrong seat-that will be an earned responsibility later. If you aren’t ready to work hard daily do not apply. 



How We Set You Up To Win (First 90 Days)

We don’t just throw you in the deep end. In your first 30 days, you’ll shadow the Ops Manager, learn our Asana + reporting systems, and get a clear scorecard so you always know what “great” looks like. By 30 days, you’ll own your own project lanes with weekly 1:1s for feedback, support, and removing blockers so you can move faster instead of guessing what we want.



Real Growth Example 

One of our Filipino teammates started with us on basic execution work at ~$800/month. Over time, he took ownership of his queue, fixed broken processes, and became the person we trusted to “just handle it.” As his scope grew, so did his comp and stability. Eight years later he makes ~$2,500/month (and we’re working on getting him even more) because he stuck with it and actually grew. A lot of people say they want that, but their resumes show 6–12 month hops. The pattern here is simple: prove you can own outcomes over time, and we grow your responsibilities, trust, and pay accordingly.



Schedule, Hours & Time Zone (No Surprises)

This is a full time, US hours role (roughly US Eastern business hours) with a true 50–60 hour workweek during this growth season. Expect most weeks to be closer to that 60 hour mark. If you want a strict 40 hour cap, this is the wrong seat; if you want a place where extra effort is noticed, measured, and rewarded, you’ll feel at home here. This is not just a job. This is a commitment.



What Winning Looks Like

By Day 30: Ops Manager is spending ~95% of his time on projects, not Slack/Asana/admin fires, because you’re handling those and executing projects alongside him. Profit and leading metrics are moving up faster because of you



By 12 months: You are Ops Manager’s go to operator & on track to become Ops Manager. Nothing important moves in Ops without you knowing. You own the Asana board, key ops projects, and reporting cadence. You’re the person we trust to “just handle it,” and your comp reflects that increased ownership. 



If you become that go to operator, you’ll have real say in how we run Ops – you won’t just be ‘executing tickets,’ you’ll help design the system.”



Who This Is NOT For

You prefer to ‘coordinate’ and assign tasks to others instead of doing the work yourself with excellence.

You want to manage people before you’ve truly proven you can personally execute at a high level. 

You want a chill, low-pressure 9–5

You need to be told what to do all day and hate being judged by objective numbers

You mark tasks complete without proof or next steps

You change jobs every 6–18 months and blame the company/manager/market/

You get defensive or freeze when given direct feedback or pressure

You are currently juggling multiple full?time clients and want to “squeeze us in” on the side.

You are mass?applying to dozens of jobs and just want to see who bites first.





Who This IS For

You’ve stayed 2–3+ years in at least one role and can prove outcomes

You like pressure, highly competitive environments, being the one who “gets it done” when others stall

You’ve built systems (trackers, automations, SOPs), not just followed them

You are tech-comfortable: Asana (or similar), CRMs, zaps, AI tools, simple web/ops/marketing stacks

You’re willing to bet on one company instead of juggling lots of smaller, easier gigs.

You’re happy to grind 50–60 hours/week no issues. We’re in a BIG growth & push season. It will be like this for the next year and then we’ll see. Everyone wants to grow a lot, but it’s actually happening here.  



Comp & Growth

Comp: Starting base $600–$700, with performance bonuses that take you to $900+ when you consistently hit + beat KPIs.” 

Raises and benefits are tied directly to beating KPIs, & raising the standard, not time served

If you crush it, scope grows into higher-level ops ownership and comp follows output

The Filipino teammate in the story above is now at ~$2,500/month and on the way up (and your growth trajectory will be much faster if you earn it because of strong systems, much better leadership, and I know what the fuck we’re doing). There is no ceiling here, this is not a forever $800 grind. But you have to earn it.  



Important: This is an ON FIELD role. You will not have a team under you to delegate to. 

95% of your time is doing the work yourself, 5% is light coordination. If your default mode is to make plans and pass tasks to others, this will be a bad fit. 

How To Apply (24-Hour Test)

Our Hiring Process (So There Are No Surprises)



If your 24 hour answers impress us, the next steps are:

A short interview focused on your past execution.

A live 60 minute work trial inside our real tools where you’ll work directly with the Ops Manager. We do this because talk is cheap. If you don’t like being tested on real work before getting hired, this won’t be a fit.



Do NOT click quick-apply. In the next 24 hours, you must:



Reply with answers to ALL of these (short but specific; bullets are fine):

Q1: Describe the most complex project you personally drove fro
ssy start to completion where you did most of the execution yourself, not just assigning tasks. Include at least one example of how you set your own deadlines and moved forward when other people were slow to respond.” 

Q2: Share 3 links or screenshots (Google Docs, Sheets, Asana boards, trackers, automations, etc.) that you built yourself which show how you organize and drive work. Briefly explain each.

Q3: You have 30 tasks due this week and realize you’ll miss 5. Walk me through, step-by-step, how you handle it with your manager and stakeholders.

Q4:  Below are 6 messy “tasks” we actually see (all dumped into one list):

– “Fix Asana, it’s a mess”

– “Seller lead texting follow up??”

– “Finance com/projections cadence d2 ”

– “Inventory backlog insane”

– “Need better reporting”

– “Update SOPs

In this role you will NOT have anyone to delegate to assume it’s just you and the Ops Manager.

In a Google Doc, please:



Rewrite these into clear tasks with: Owner (you or Ops Manager), Due Date (next 7–30 days), and a concrete Done Check + proof required. “Write your task descriptions as if you are committing: ‘I will do X by Y time. If Z doesn’t happen by [time], here’s my fallback.’ Generic ‘follow up / request access’ answers will fail you.” 

Put them in the order you’d actually do them and explain why in 3–5 bullet points.

Link the Google Doc here (view access).

Spend no more than 30–45 minutes. If you can’t figure this out on your own, this role will be too hard in real life – that’s okay, just skip applying.



Attach your PDF resume/Google Drive link.



Compensation here is performance based. Raises are earned through clearly exceeding KPIs and demonstrating core values consistently. If you want “stability” to mean “I can coast and still get raises,” this won’t feel stable. title: Remote Senior Nonprofit Bookkeeper
description:
About Us

We are a USA-based accounting and advisory firm dedicated exclusively to serving nonprofit organizations and mental health practices. We manage the complete accounting cycle for a portfolio of nonprofit clients simultaneously, delivering accurate, timely, and audit-ready financial records. Our clients trust us with the financial foundation of their missions. Every tea
mber we bring on is expected to perform at a professional level from day one, follow our documented systems, and take genuine ownership of their client portfolio.



About the Role

We are seeking a highly motivated, detail-oriented Senior Bookkeeper to join our team. In this role, you will oversee comprehensive bookkeeping functions, ensuring accuracy and compliance across all financial records for a portfolio of nonprofit clients. You will work within our established systems and be held to firm-wide standards of accuracy and deadlines from day one.



This is not an entry-level role. You are expected to arrive with a fully developed competency in nonprofit accounting and the professional judgment to apply it independently across multiple clients in a remote environment.



Responsibilities

- Record and classify all transactions on an accrual basis with proper account coding, class tracking, and fund designation.

- Manage and maintain the general ledger in accordance with GAAP.

- Manage accounts payable and accounts receivable: enter vendor bills, process payments, record invoices, and apply receipts accurately.

- Prepare and post all month-end journal entries, including accruals, prepaid amortization, depreciation, and deferred revenue schedules.

- Conduct balance sheet reconciliation and review financial statements for discrepancies or errors.

- Record payroll allocation entries across cost centers, grants, and functional expense categories.

- Track restricted grants, donor contributions, and program expenses in compliance with nonprofit accounting standards.

- Produce and deliver month-end financial statements for management review.

- Support the Form 990 and audit preparation process by maintaining clean, organized records and preparing schedules as requested.

- Maintain meticulous records of journal entries, account analyses, and audit documentation to ensure audit readiness.

- Utilize accounting software, including QuickBooks Online and Xero, to manage bookkeeping operations.

- Identify opportunities to automate financial processes and increase efficiency.

- Deliver clear, accurate financial reports for internal review, client communication, and external audits.



Qualifications

 - Minimum 5 years of nonprofit accounting experience with demonstrated ability to apply accrual accounting, fund accounting, net asset classifications under ASU
, grant tracking, and functional expense allocation independently and without supervision.

 - Demonstrated ability to apply ASC 606 and ASC 842 standards, specifically managing revenue recognition based on grant documents, funder restrictions, and milestones.

- Experience managing multiple clients simultaneously in an outsourced accounting firm or agency setting.

- Advanced proficiency in QuickBooks Online (QBO), Xero, Sage, and other financial management tools.

- Advanced proficiency in project and work management tools such as Asana, Gmail, Google Sheets, Microsoft Excel, 
, Ramp, and similar platforms.

- Deep understanding of GAAP, double-entry bookkeeping, bank reconciliation, and general ledger reconciliation.

- Familiarity with governmental accounting practices and tax experience is highly desirable.

- Excellent knowledge of financial concepts, including account analysis, account reconciliation, debits and credits, journal entries, and balance sheet management.

- Ability to context-shift between multiple clients and thrive in a fast-paced, remote environment.

- Strong attention to detail and analytical skills to interpret complex financial data accurately.

- Effective written communication skills for financial reporting and client correspondence.

- High integrity, accountability, and respect for client confidentiality.

- Minimum 12 consecutive months of fully remote, self-directed work with independent deadline management.

- Problem-solving mentality with a proactive approach to process improvement and continuous learning.



Schedule and Compensation

- Part-time: 15 hours per week, with required availability between 8:00 AM and 3:00 PM EST // 9 pm and 2 am Philippines time. Hours are expected to increase to full-time as performance benchmarks are met, and the client portfolio grows

- Compensation details: $8 per hour for a trial period (1-3 months) and $10 per hour (post-trial period) 



To Apply: To be considered for this position, your application must include the following, submitted together in a single
:

 - Your resume

 - A brief message describing your experience with nonprofit fund accounting and at least one outsourced or multi-client accounting environment you have supported

- The answer to the following question, included at the top of your message: "What is the net asset classification framework introduced under ASU
, and how does it differ from the previous two-category model?"



Applications that do not follow these instructions exactly will not be reviewed.

title: Night-Shift Remote Security Monitoring VA (x2 Positions)
description:
We're a 27-year-old Australian technology company providing security and facility management solutions to the self-storage industry across Australia, New Zealand, and Asia. We're launching a new remote monitoring service — a live overnight security layer for self-storage operators — and we're hiring two VAs to run it. This is not a support or admin role. You are the live human response between an alarm firing and a client walking into a damaged facility in the morning.



Hours & Setup



Hours: Full-time — approximately 40 hours per week

Shift: 9:00 pm – 6:00 am AEST, Monday to Friday

Location: Remote — Philippines-based candidates

Positions: Two roles — both working the same shift, onboarded together

Growth: This is a pilot with a 25-site client. As the service scales to additional operators (5–10 expected to follow quickly), the team grows with it. The first two hires set the standard the product is judged by.





What You'll Be Doing

Camera Monitoring & Facility Sweeps



Conduct structured camera sweeps across assigned self-storage facilities throughout your shift

Complete 4–5 full sweep cycles per facility per shift — reviewing all active camera feeds each time

Monitor for unauthorised access, suspicious activity, fence breaches, or movement anomalies during non-operating hours

Apply judgement to distinguish real security threats from benign triggers (bin trucks, authorised access, weather)

Log every sweep via our check-in reporting tool: timestamp, cameras reviewed, status, and notes



Alarm Response & Real-Time Escalation



Act as the first live point of contact when an alarm event triggers at an assigned facility

Receive notifications from the alarm monitoring company and immediately pull up relevant camera footage

Assess in real time: active break-in, suspicious activity, or false alarm

For confirmed or suspected break-ins in progress — call police immediately with live camera confirmation, then work through the facility's call register

For false alarms — log the event with timestamp, footage reference, and a brief description; no further escalation required

Follow the pre-assigned call register for each site — every facility has its own escalation contacts



I
 Reporting & Morning Handover



Complete a structured shift report for each assigned facility using our reporting tool

Upload screenshots or footage stills as supporting evidence for any i
 or flagged activity

Produce a consolidated morning summary per client: all events, outcomes, and recommended follow-up

Ensure all reports are complete and ready before shift end — the client's morning report should be in their inbox before their day starts

Maintain a consistent, professional reporting standard every single shift — these reports are our proof of service



Communication & Team Coordination



Answer inbound calls from the alarm monitoring company during events

Communicate clearly and calmly by phone with Australian police and facility contacts when escalating

Coordinate with the second monitoring VA on handovers, shared coverage, and volume spikes

Flag camera outages, system issues, or platform problems to the internal technical team immediately

Maintain working knowledge of assigned facilities, camera counts, access configurations, and site-specific sensitivities



Ongoing Operational Input



Contribute to SOP documentation as the monitoring service is refined through the pilot

Provide feedback on reporting tool functionality, sweep efficiency, and any process gaps

Participate in team briefings as the service evolves and new client sites come online





What We're Looking For

Experience



Prior experience in security monitoring, surveillance, CCTV operations, dispatch, or a similar operations role is preferred — but not a hard requirement if you can demonstrate the right instincts

Proven ability to work independently through an overnight shift without direct supervision

Demonstrated capacity to stay focused and alert during extended periods of low activity — this is the core working condition

Background in customer service, operations, or communications is an advantage



Technical Skills



Comfortable navigating CCTV camera dashboards and multi-camera interfaces (full platform training provided)

Able to operate a VoIP softphone for inbound and outbound calls during events

Basic computer literacy:
 (Google Workspace), reporting tools, and team communication platforms

Familiarity with any of the following is a plus: Sightline, HikVision, Storm, or Freshdesk — but not required

Dual-screen setup recommended; must have a reliable internet connection and quality headset



Communication & Work Style



Strong verbal English — you will be calling Australian police and facility contacts during active alarm events; this is not the 
nt for unclear communication

Strong written English — morning reports and i
 summaries go directly to clients; they must be professional and complete

Calm and composed under pressure — the most important call of the shift may come at 3 am

Reliable shift attendance is non-negotiable; if you're not on shift, facilities are unmonitored

This must be your primary, focused commitment — not suitable for combining with study or competing evening obligations





You'll Thrive Here If You Are…

Genuinely alert overnight. You don't fight the shift — you're wired for it. Quiet hours aren't downtime; they're the job.

Calm when it counts. When the alarm fires at 3 am, you look at the footage, make the call, and follow the process. You don't freeze or overthink under pressure.

Detail-obsessed. You notice the figure at the edge of the frame, the door that should be closed, the movement that doesn't add up. You catch what others scroll past.

Methodical, every single shift. You run the same sweep, to the same standard, whether it's a busy Friday night or a dead-quiet Tuesday. No shortcuts during the easy shifts.

Proactively a logger. You don't sit on a decision. You document immediately, flag anything off, and don't wait to be told during an active event.

Accountable by default. You understand that the client service promise rests on your presence and your performance. You show up, every shift, on time.

Sound in your judgement. You know the difference between a bin truck and a break-in without needing a flowchart. You escalate when it matters — and only when it matters.



To Apply

Google Maps

Google Sheets

Gmail

Reliable internet connection

Able to start lead research and outreach immediately

Available to work during agreed hours and submit daily reports



Experience working with marketing agencies, restaurants, med spas, local businesses, or hospitality brands is a plus.



This is not a role for someone who needs to learn basic lead generation from the beginning.



Performance Expectations



This is a results-focused outbound lead generation role.



You will be given our target industries, offer details, outreach guidelines, and message templates. However, you must already know how to find leads, research businesses, send outreach messages, follow up, and book appointments.



This is not a paid training role. You are expected to start finding leads and sending outreach from your first working day.



You will be responsible for finding your own leads using sources such as:



Google Maps

Instagram

Business websites

Online directories

Local business searches

Appointment Goal



The minimum requirement for this role is:



5 qualified appointments per week



Appointment quality matters. We do not want rando
etings, fake interest, or unqualified leads. We only want meetings with real business owners, managers, marketing directors, general managers, or decision-makers who may be a good fit for WA Media’s social media management and content creation services.



A meeting is only considered qualified if the prospect:



Has a real business

Fits our target industries

Is a decision-maker or can connect us directly to the decision-maker

Understands the meeting is about WA Media’s social media/content services

Agrees to a specific meeting time

Shows up to the meeting



Meetings that do not show up, are not a good fit, or were booked using misleading information will not count toward the weekly appointment requirement or bonus opportunities.



Pay

Starting pay is $5/hour

This role will start at 20 hours per week

There is room to increase hours and pay based on performance, reliability, quality of work, and results

We also offer multiple bonus opportunities based on qualified appointments, strong monthly performance, and closed clients



Bonus details will be discussed with selected applicants.



Schedule

Part-time to start: 20 hours per week

Preferred schedule will be discussed

We prefer someone who can work consistently Monday through Friday

Some overlap with Pacific Time is preferred, especially for communication and meeting coordination

At the end of each workday, you will submit a report with:



Hours worked

Number of new leads researched

Number of outreach messages sent

Number of follow-ups sent

Positive replies

Meetings booked

Best leads of the day

Questions or issues

We want someone who is consistent, honest, organized, and motivated.

You must be comfortable finding your own leads each day instead of waiting for us to provide a list.



If you do well, this can grow into a long-term role with more hours, higher pay, bonuses, and more responsibility.



How to Apply

Your experience with lead generation or appointment setting

Your experience finding your own leads

Your experience using Instagram, Google Maps, Gmail, and Google Sheets

Your expected hourly rate

Your availability and preferred work schedule

Applications without a video introduction will not be considered.

title: Virtual Assistant, Operations Expert for Career Coaching & Speaking Practice Remote |
description:
Virtual Assistant, Operations Expert for Career Coaching & Speaking Practice

Remote | Philippines-Based | Part-Time to Full-Time





Most VA job posts want someone who is good at following instructions.



This one is a bit different.



Yes, there are tasks. Research to do. Resumes to reformat. Asana and CRM to manage. Outreach
s to send. 



But the person who thrives here isn't just executing a checklist, I need someone who looks at a half-finished process and, excitedly, thinks "I can make this better." Someone who catches a problem before being asked. Someone who takes ownership and runs with it.



If that's how you work, keep reading.





About the Role

You'll work directly with a U.S.-based career coach and keynote speaker — a one-person practice with a growing pipeline and no signs of slowing down. The work is varied and won't repeat itself. One week, you're processing 50+ post-event survey responses and running segmented outreach. The next, you're reformatting a resume that could change someone's career trajectory, or finalizing content for an upcoming speaking engagement.



Every workflow has a Loom walkthrough, a custom AI prompt, or a written doc behind it. You'll never be guessing what "done" looks like. But documentation is a starting point — once you know a process, you're expected to make it better.



This starts at 20 hours a week. The path to 40 hours is there, and it's based on one thing: trust earned through consistent work, communication, and process improvement.





What You'll Actually Do

Resume & Career Documents 

Reformat and polish resumes in Microsoft Word using custom AI prompts

Convert resumes into LinkedIn summaries, cover letters, and other career documents

Use AI tools to produce clean, human-sounding output — not raw generated text dropped into a template



Speaking & Event Operations

Process post-event
 campaigns: sort 50+ audience survey responses, send segmented outreach by response type

Conduct LinkedIn outreach to event attendees using provided templates

Track pre- and post-talk logistics in Asana



Content & Social

Schedule and publish content on LinkedIn and other platforms

Take 70%-complete drafts and get them ready to publish — close the gaps, fix the formatting, make it land



Business Development Support

Support B2B outreach to wealth management firms and companies going through layoffs

Help maintain outreach sequences and track pipeline activity



Operations & Reporting

Manage Asana daily: update task statuses, flag what needs attention, keep dashboards current

Send daily and weekly activity reports — the owner should always know what's moving





Who You Are

You write English at a professional level and you've actually worked with AI tools — meaning you know how to take generated output and make it sound like a person wrote it.



You're organized in a way that shows up in your work, not just how you describe yourself. You finish things. When something's stuck, you say so before it becomes a problem. When a process is unclear, you ask one sharp question and move forward.



You're comfortable working async. You don't need daily check-ins to stay on track.





Required:



Comfortable learning from Loom videos and async documentation

Professional written English

Asana or similar project management experience

Real experience with Claude (my preferred AI of choice) — with the judgment to refine output, not just use it

Google Suite and Microsoft Office proficiency for document formatting

Experience managing LinkedIn or other social platforms

Reliable high-speed internet and a dedicated home office setup



Bonus:

Background in career coaching, staffing, or HR

B2B outreach or lead generation experience

Experience with content calendars or social scheduling tools





Compensation & Schedule

Hourly: $8–$10 USD 

Hours: 20 hrs/week to start, path to 40 hrs 

Schedule: Flexible async with 2–3 hours daily overlap at 2:00 PM Pacific (5:00 AM Philippine Time) 

Start: ASAP





Before You Apply

Know you won't be thrown in without context. There are Loom walkthroughs, documented workflows, and AI prompts for the tasks that need them. The systems are there and being updated. 



I welcome any and all recommendations, tools, hacks, and automations. I want both of us to work smarter, not just harder. 



If you want a role where you wait for instructions, I don’t think this will be a good fit.



If you want to have input and ownership of the day to day, grow into a bigger role, and become a key part of growth and strategy, please apply!

title: Financial Accountant - AU Company
description:
Who is Bare?

Bare is the new way to funeral. We are a holistic end of life care provider, allowing our families to grieve in their own way, at their own pace, knowing their loved one is cared for by a team who truly understand their needs.



By combining empathy with technology, we’re creating end-of-life experiences that are simple, personalized and affordable. In only five years, we’ve served more than 30,000 families, have become Australia’s most awarded end-of-life provider (with awards in customer service, innovation and digital disruption), and have built a team of more than 100 people committed to changing the way Australians deal with end-of-life. And we’re just getting started.



We’re looking for a passionate and detail-oriented Financial Accountant to join our high-performing remote team. If you're a proactive finance professional who thrives on ownership, continuous improvement, and meaningful work, we’d love to meet you.



What You’ll Be Doing

As our Financial Accountant, you’ll be a key player in ensuring accurate, insightful, and timely financial reporting. You’ll collaborate across teams, drive process improvement, and uphold the financial integrity of our mission.



Key Responsibilities:

-Own the Month-End Close

Lead all aspects of EOM: journal entries, reconciliations, accruals, and financial statement prep.

-Deliver Insightful Reporting

Produce monthly and quarterly management reports, including variance and trend analysis.

-Ensure Regulatory Compliance

Prepare BAS, IAS, and statutory filings, ensuring alignment with AASB and tax standards.

-Champion Continuous Improvement

Streamline workflows, introduce automation, and enhance internal controls.

-Collaborate Cross-Functionally

Partner with Marketing, Operations, and other non-finance teams to align on budget and strategy.

-Support Strategic Projects

Get involved in cost analysis, ERP upgrades, and special projects that shape our financial future.



Why Join Bare?

Make a Meaningful Impact: Your work directly supports families during one of the most vulnerable times of their lives.

Remote-First Flexibility: Work from anywhere in Australia with the tools and autonomy to succeed.

Mission-Driven Culture: Join a team that leads with empathy and integrity—where your voice matters.

Growth & Innovation: Help shape scalable systems in a business that's growing fast and disrupting the norm.



About You

You’re not just technically sharp, you bring heart and high standards to everything you do. You thrive in fast-paced environments and care about doing work that matters.



Must-Haves:

-Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or similar.

-CPA/CA qualification (or in-progress).

-2–3+ years' experience in financial accounting, ideally in service-led sectors.

-Familiarity with Australian accounting standards, BAS/IAS, and financial reporting.

-Understanding of various accounting standards relevant to Bare and consolidations of many entities.

-Attention to detail and excellent reconciliation skills

-Strong ERP (MYOB, Xero, SAP) and Excel skills.

-Strong Excel/Sheets skills and automation of manual processes in your mindset-DNA



Nice-to-Haves:

• Experience in mission-driven sectors (healthcare, aged care, funeral services).

• Adaptability in high-growth or high-volume environments.

• Resilient, working with little or no supervision.

• Experience of managing international teams, interaction with multi-entity organizations, and experience within companies with a minimum annual revenue of $50 million.

• Handle ambiguity, competing priorities, and strict deadlines. Create and implement scalable processes, including training. Integrate AI and automation.



Core Values We Look For

• Empathy: You care deeply about people—colleagues and customers alike.

• Accountability: You take ownership and deliver results with pride.

• Clarity: You communicate financial information in a clear, human way.

• Curiosity: You’re always looking for a better way and love solving problems.



Perks & Benefits

-Fully remote work setup with flexible hours

-Purpose-driven work with real human impact

-Growth and learning opportunities in a scale-up environment

-Supportive, inclusive team culture



Please include your resume when submitting your application. Thank you!
